en: Therīgāthā 6.1 Chakkanipāta:
The Five Hundred Verses of the Elder Nuns (Pañcasatamattātherīgāthā)
“Of that being from whom you do not know the path—
whether of its coming or its going—
from where has that being come?”
"You cry out, 'My son!
yet you know neither the path by which he came nor the path by which he went."
Do not grieve for him,
for such is the nature of living beings;
he has gone away uninvited.
He did not depart from here without being permitted;
surely he must have come from somewhere else and stayed for a few days.
Having gone from here by one way,
he goes from there by another;
though deceased, he appears in human form.
Wandering through saṃsāra, he will go on;
as he came, so he has gone—
what cause for lamentation is there in that?
“Truly, you have pulled out the arrow for me—
That which was lodged in my heart and so difficult to see—
For me, who was overcome by sorrow.”
She has dispelled the grief for her son.
Today, with the arrow extracted,
she is free from craving and has attained final Nibbāna.
“I go for refuge to the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha, to the Sage.
Thus it was that five hundred elder bhikkhunīs... [and so forth].
